claims.text:
Holman means "hole-man", and is distinct from the real-life English surname which contains holm "river island" rather than hol "hole".
Category:HobbitsCategory:Cotton
Category:Third Age characters
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Nomenclature of The Lord of the Rings" in Wayne G. Hammond and Christina Scull (eds), The Lord of the Rings: A Reader's Companion, p. 760

claims.text: Holman means "hole-man", and is distinct from the real-life English surname which contains holm "river island" rather than hol "hole".
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Nomenclature of The Lord of the Rings" in Wayne G. Hammond and Christina Scull (eds), The Lord of the Rings: A Reader's Companion, p. 760

claims.text: Holman was the son of Cotman. He moved to Bywater, and took up the family name "Cotton". He became a farmer, which passed to his son, Tom. He also had another son, Will.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix C, "The Longfather-tree of Master Samwise"
